title: Functions
intro: Serverless functions: handlers written for AWS Lambda™ (Node.js, Python) run on this server, in an isolated container started on demand. The same code also runs on AWS Lambda without changes.
trademarkNotice: AWS Lambda is a trademark of Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates. Loch.sh is not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon.
disabled: The functions module is disabled on this server (FUNCTIONS_ENABLED).
configError: The functions module is enabled but could not start: see the API logs.
runtimeNotReady: No trusted function runtime is installed on the server yet: functions cannot be created or run.
limitReached: The limit of {{max}} functions is reached: delete a function first.

presentation.title: No function yet
presentation.text: A function is a handler (index.handler, lambda_function.lambda_handler) uploaded as a zip, with its dependencies. The panel runs it in the AWS Lambda base image published by AWS, with the memory, CPU and timeout you choose; sites, services and other functions on its networks invoke it with the AWS SDK or a plain HTTP request.
presentation.security: Each function gets its own private network, no published port and no Internet access unless you allow it; its invoke credentials are shown once.

runtimeDescriptions.nodejs: JavaScript or TypeScript compiled to JavaScript.
runtimeDescriptions.provided: Any compiled language: a bootstrap executable built for Linux.

stateHints.not_deployed: Created, but no code was uploaded yet: nothing runs.
stateHints.running: The function's container runs and answers invocations.
stateHints.stopped: The function is stopped: start it to invoke it.
stateHints.missing: Code is deployed and the function is not stopped, but its container does not exist: start it again.
stateHints.modified: Its compose project was edited outside the panel: the panel never runs it. Purge it.
stateHints.unverified: A container runs, but it is not the one the panel created: it is not used.
stateHints.invalid: Its reference file is unreadable: it can only be purged.

egress.label: Internet access
egress.onHint: The function can reach the Internet (and the host, the LAN and metadata endpoints unless firewall rules say otherwise).
egress.offHint: The function only reaches the members of its networks.
egress.help: Off by default: the function only reaches the members of its networks.
egress.warning: With Internet access, the function's code can send its data and secrets anywhere, and reach the host gateway, the LAN and cloud metadata endpoints unless DOCKER-USER firewall rules block them.
egress.recreate: The function's container is recreated: an invocation in progress is cut.

sigv4.label: SigV4 callers (AWS SDK)
sigv4.bearer: Callers always authenticate with a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer …), shown once.
sigv4.help: Off by default. On: AWS SDK clients can also invoke the function with an access key pair (endpoint-url http://fn-<name>:8080, region us-east-1).
sigv4.warning: The runtime needs the SigV4 secret itself: it is in the container, so the function's code can read it. It only lets the function be invoked.

stop.title: Stop {{name}}?
stop.content: The function no longer answers invocations until it is started again (scheduled tasks fail meanwhile).

restart.title: Restart {{name}}?
restart.content: Its container is restarted: invocations in progress are cut.

delete.title: Delete the function {{name}}?
delete.content: Its container, code, every deployment, secrets, invoke credentials and its own network are deleted. Nothing can be recovered.

purge.title: Purge the function {{name}}?
purge.content: The function was edited outside the panel: it is removed without running any of its files (containers, code, deployments, secrets, credentials). Nothing can be recovered.

toasts.networkKept: The network {{network}} was kept: other members are still attached to it.

create.title: New function
create.intro: A function runs a handler written for AWS Lambda™. Nothing runs until its code is deployed: upload a zip now or later from its page.
create.imageNote: AWS Lambda base image published by AWS for {{arch}}, pulled through mirror.gcr.io and pinned by digest.
create.handlerInvalid: <file>.<function>: letters, digits, _ and -, folders separated by /, e.g. index.handler or src/app.handler.

handlerHelp.nodejs: <file>.<export>, e.g. index.handler for the handler exported by index.js (or index.mjs).
handlerHelp.provided: Passed to your bootstrap as _HANDLER, which it may read. Empty: bootstrap.

create.zipOptional: Optional: the handler and its dependencies, never built on the server. It is uploaded right after the creation.

code.title: Code
code.subtitle: The handler the runtime calls, and optionally the zip to deploy.

env.title: Variables and secrets
env.subtitle: Environment of the function. Secrets are kept apart and can never be read back.

networks.title: Network access
networks.subtitle: Who can invoke the function, and what it can reach.

invoke.title: Invocation
invoke.subtitle: How callers on its networks authenticate.

name.title: Name
name.subtitle: 1 to {{max}} lowercase letters, digits or dashes, starting with a letter. It is also its hostname: fn-<name>.

create.nameInvalid: 1 to 21 lowercase letters, digits or dashes, starting with a letter and not ending with a dash.
create.nameTaken: A function with this name already exists.

summary.title: Summary
summary.name: Name
summary.credentialsNote: The invoke credentials are shown once, right after the creation.

setup.title: Setting up
setup.failed: Failed: {{error}} Do it again from the function's page.

create.handlerInvalidCustom: Letters, digits, _, - and ., folders separated by /, no part starting with . or -; at most 128 characters.

bootstrap.title: The zip holds a bootstrap executable at its root
bootstrap.help: Build it for Linux {{arch}} and zip it, for example in Go with aws-lambda-go:

resources.tmpNote: Files in /tmp count against the memory limit: a function filling /tmp is stopped for lack of memory.
resources.budget: Still available for the functions: {{memory}} of memory and {{cpus}} CPU.
resources.overBudget: These resources exceed what is left of the functions' budget: the creation will be refused.

env.nameInvalid: Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.
env.nameReserved: This name is reserved by the runtime (AWS_LAMBDA_*, AWS_REGION, PATH…).
env.nameDuplicate: This name is already used by a variable or a secret.

variable.title: Variables
variable.help: Written in the function's compose file: do not put secrets here.

secret.title: Secrets
secret.warning: A secret value is written once: it can be replaced or removed, never shown again, by the panel or anyone.

networks.title: Networks
networks.intro: Members of these networks (sites, service instances, other functions) can invoke the function at its internal URL. A function never joins the services network.
networks.dedicatedHint: Created with the function, only for it: attach the sites or services that invoke it.
networks.extraHelp: Optional: networks the function also joins.
networks.servicesRefused: A function never joins the services network: attach it to a private network.
networks.connectIntro: The function's container is recreated with this network: an invocation in progress is cut.
networks.noneAvailable: The function is already on every private network.

disconnectConfirm.title: Disconnect {{name}} from {{network}}?
disconnectConfirm.content: The network is cut first, then the container is recreated: the members of this network can no longer invoke the function. If the recreation fails, the function is stopped.

networks.lastHint: A function keeps at least one network: connect another one first.
networks.notConnectedHint: The function's container is not on this network: it is stopped, or must be restarted.

detail.notFound: This function does not exist (any more).

overview.endpointHint: Reachable only by the members of the function's networks, with its credentials (POST, the event as body).
overview.notDeployed: No code is deployed yet: upload a zip in the Code tab.
overview.modified: Its compose project was edited outside the panel, so the panel never runs it again. Restore the file the panel rendered, or purge the function.
overview.invalid: Its reference file is unreadable: the panel cannot use it. Purge the function.
overview.unverified: A container runs, but it does not match the function's reference: the panel does not use it. Restart the function to recreate it.

code.uploadIntro: A zip with the handler ({{handler}}) and its dependencies at its root. It becomes a new deployment, activated at once; if it does not start, the previous one is started again.
code.drop: Drop a zip here, or click to choose one
code.dropHint: At most {{max}}. Only stored and deflated entries; no encrypted entry, device or link leaving the archive.
code.kept_one: {{count}} deployment is kept, the active one included.
code.kept_other: {{count}} deployments are kept for a rollback, the active one included.

activateConfirm.title: Activate deployment {{id}}?
activateConfirm.content: Its files are verified, then the function is recreated with them: an invocation in progress is cut.

rollbackConfirm.title: Roll back to deployment {{id}}?
rollbackConfirm.content: The function goes back to this older code (verified first): an invocation in progress is cut. The current deployment is kept.

code.interrupted: Upload interrupted: the server may still have deployed the code, check the deployments list.
code.uploadIntroCustom: A zip with the bootstrap executable at its root, built for Linux {{arch}}. It becomes a new deployment, activated at once; if it does not start, the previous one is started again.

test.eventHelp: One JSON value (object, array, string, number…), passed to the handler as its event.
test.notRunning: The function is not running: start it before invoking it.

configuration.deployScope: The handler and the variables decide what the code does with its secrets: with an API key, changing them needs the functions:deploy scope as well as functions:write.

confirm.title: Save the configuration of {{name}}?
confirm.running: The function is recreated with it: an invocation in progress is cut.
confirm.stopped: The function stays stopped: the configuration applies at its next start.

mcp.title: AI assistants (MCP)
mcp.label: Invocable by MCP clients
mcp.help: A guard-rail for the MCP tool of the loch CLI (AI assistants): when off, the tool refuses to invoke this function. It is not an access control: to forbid invocations, give the MCP client an API key without the functions:invoke scope. Changing it needs the functions:deploy scope.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.intro: Secrets are passed to the function as environment variables, kept outside its compose file. Their values are never shown, returned, logged nor audited: replace a value to change it.

removeConfirm.title: Remove the secret {{name}}?
removeConfirm.content: The function no longer receives it: it is recreated.

secrets.restart: The running function is recreated with it.

credentials.title: Invoke credentials
credentials.warning: Copy these credentials now: they are shown only once. The panel keeps only what checks them and cannot show them again; rotate them if they are lost.
credentials.curl: Copy a test command (curl, from a member of its networks)
credentials.internalOnly: The internal URL is reachable only from the members of the function's networks: it has no published port.
credentials.sigv4Note: AWS SDK: endpoint-url http://fn-<name>:8080, region us-east-1, with this key pair.

credentialsTab.title: Invoke credentials
credentialsTab.intro: Callers on the function's networks authenticate with these credentials; the panel's own invocations (Test tab, scheduled tasks) need none. They cannot be read again: rotate them to get new ones.

rotate.title: Rotate the credentials of {{name}}?
rotate.content: New credentials are generated and shown once; the current ones stop working at once. The function is recreated.

enableSigv4.title: Accept SigV4 callers for {{name}}?
enableSigv4.content: The credentials are rotated: a new bearer token and a SigV4 key pair are shown once, the current ones stop working.

disableSigv4.title: Stop accepting SigV4 callers for {{name}}?
disableSigv4.content: The credentials are rotated without a key pair: a new bearer token is shown once, the current credentials stop working.

triggers.title: Scheduled invocations
triggers.intro: Scheduled tasks of type “Function invocation” targeting this function (at most {{max}}).
triggers.empty: No scheduled task invokes this function.

deploymentWarnings.FUNCTION_BOOTSTRAP_DYNAMIC: The bootstrap is dynamically linked against glibc: it runs only if it was built against a glibc no newer than Amazon Linux 2023's. Build it statically (CGO_ENABLED=0) to avoid this.
